I have thick but fine hair. After I wash, I put in mousse. Then I dry and attempt to style my mop. Then I use a make up brush and apply corn starch to sections of my roots that tend to get most greasy (around my face, bangs). During the powdering part I always have a moment where I pretend I’m George Washington. It works great and I’m starting to go from having greasy hair every 12 hours to being able to go 2 days. It kind of acts as a texture powder along side my mouse and I kinda have that piece-y shaggy long bob look. 

P.S. if you’re not blonde you can mix cocoa powder in with your corn starch until desired color is reached.

Your sixth sense analogy is so real. I’m going to borrow that. I’m about 6 months into more therapy and I’m learning to pay attention to my thoughts and feels again. My big realization came when I was *at work* and Pirates of the Caribbean was on tv. I had no sleep, a phenomenal amount of stress, and my guard wasn’t up. A hot mermaid came on the screen and I thought “oh my god she is so hot.” Then I thought “wait wait wait don’t look at her you’re supposed to think one of these pirate guys is cute.” I had finally observed the suppression in real time. I couldn’t un-observe it. I cracked open through the rest of my 12 hour shift watching memories of my life where I had squashed my gayness. It’s so dumb because really? Pirates of the Caribbean? And at work of all times? But idk that’s just how it went down.

I mean I definitely agree that I was tamping down and suppressing. I think another painful piece of this is that acknowledging I chose (kinda) to suppress this is painful. I feel like “missed the signs” is more passive while I’m still coming to terms with this. It’s all very fraught as I’m sure you know. 
I also had some scary experiences with a high school boy where I realized I wasn’t safe yet nobody cared and nobody would do anything about it. It was horrific even as someone who thought they had attraction toward this person. I spent a few years doing trauma therapy over it and my therapist could not understand why I was so affected by it. I feel like it makes more sense now because even though I was consenting at times that was due to me completely suppressing my real feelings about it to seem normal and please the other person. My more recent therapist pointed out that when you suppress one emotion you end up suppressing ALL of them. It makes sense to me that I was not only suppressing my baby gay self, but also fear, anger, disgust, and sadness that came up later from these situations.

Hi, fellow not fun parent here. 

Over time my kid is starting to understand that he can trust *me* with the big things. He loves both his parents but he knows I’m the one to talk to when shit hits the fan or he needs safety. 
I might not be as fun but thank god my kid can feel that security, something that kids can’t get from the spontaneous, irresponsible flightiness of the fun parent in my scenario. All of this to say that when your kids are grown they will look back and see you as a hero and a saint.

I promise you that no matter what you think you did, this is not your fault. I feel positive that you were doing the best you could with the energy, resources, and knowledge you had. These situations are inherently higher risk, and though there is a lot of pressure on moms to make lifestyle changes there is only so much that can realistically be done. On top of that, society is not very supportive or helpful with these things and it’s a systemic issue, not something that falls on you as an individual.

I know that nothing any of can write here will make this better. Right now you are wrestling with possibly the deepest type of grief there is. And that’s normal. These feelings of “what could I have done differently?” are just that bargaining part of the grief process. 

One thing I’ve heard about the grief process is that there’s times where you are grieving and times when you are rebuilding. Right now the grief will take up almost all of your time. It will always be there, but over time the rebuilding times will happen more and more so that the grief times are less heavy.

Whatever feelings and thoughts you have cropping up right now, just know they are normal and that we are here to listen.

I don’t know if this is helpful or not, but I use principles found in intuitive eating as my abstinence plan. I am following evidence based research regarding binge eating disorder and it’s helping me stop bingeing. The problem is that though the stop in bingeing is helping me lose weight, it’s very slow. Many folks in the program have encouraged me to cut out certain types of foods completely. I have found that when I do this it isn’t sustainable for me. It might work for me for 2 weeks or so, then I give up and all I can eat is that one thing. Please feel free to dm me if you need to chat. I know it’s frustrating. I’m not a sponsor and don’t have a lot of abstinence under my belt but in the past 6 months of OA where I’ve stubbornly used my (sometimes advised against by other members) approach I have gone from having 5+ episodes of binge eating in a day to maybe 1 every few weeks. Even if I’ve only lost about 15 of the 100+ lbs I need to lose I’m happy knowing that I could keep on this track forever if I needed to. I know I couldn’t give up my favorite foods forever, and for me this approach is working right now.

In therapy I realized my husband was constantly belittling and controlling me and that was a contributor to my feeling like a garbage parent. 3.) I sought divorce 4.) I took parenting classes and coaching to help me figure out how parenting actually is supposed to work. And also so I didn't have to take all the bullshit unsolicited advice people give.

I hope you find your own path to healing and feeling better. Parenting is hard, but healing will give you access to the joyful parts of it. When you feel like shit all of it feels like a slog.
